results.name: Band Single Arm Pec Fly
instructions: Attach a resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at chest height. Stand facing away from the anchor point, holding the handle of the band in your working hand with your arm extended out to the side, palm facing forward.
Keep your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and your chest engaged.
Pull the band in an arc motion, bringing your hand towards the center of your chest.
Slowly return your arm to the starting position. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
tips: Engage your core to stabilize your body and prevent unnecessary movement.
Use a controlled motion to pull and return the band, preventing any jerking movements.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you pull the band across your body and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
Keep your elbow slightly bent throughout the movement to avoid joint strain.
results.description: Band Single Arm Pec Fly is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

results.name: Barbell Bench Press Decline
instructions: Set a decline bench at a suitable angle and lie down on it with your feet secured under the foot pads. Grip the barbell with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and unrack the barbell by extending your arms fully. Lower the barbell slowly and with control to your lower chest, keeping your elbows at a 90-degree angle to your body.
Press the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your arms fully, focusing on using your chest muscles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then carefully rack the barbell back onto the bench press rack.
tips: Keep your feet secured under the foot pads to maintain stability and prevent sliding.
Engage your core to maintain a stable and strong torso throughout the movement.
Lower the barbell slowly and with control to prevent injury and maximize muscle engagement.
results.description: Barbell Bench Press Decline is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Barbell Incline Bench Press (Front View)
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 45 degree angle and lie down on it with your feet flat on the floor. Grip the barbell with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and unrack the barbell by extending your arms fully. Lower the barbell slowly and with control to your upper chest, keeping your elbows at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Press the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your arms fully, focusing on using your chest muscles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then carefully rack the barbell back onto the bench press rack.
tips: Keep your feet flat on the floor to maintain stability and support your lower back.
Engage your core to maintain a stable and strong torso throughout the movement.
Lower the barbell slowly and with control to prevent injury and maximize muscle engagement.
results.description: Barbell Incline Bench Press (Front View) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Barbell Bench Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor. Grip the barbell with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, and position the bar directly above your chest.
Engage your core and unrack the barbell by extending your arms fully. Lower the barbell slowly and with control to your chest, keeping your elbows at a 90-degree angle to your body.
Press the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your arms fully, focusing on using your chest muscles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then carefully rack the barbell back onto the bench press rack.
tips: Keep your feet flat on the floor to maintain stability and support your lower back.
Engage your core to maintain a stable and strong torso throughout the movement.
Lower the barbell slowly and with control to prevent injury and maximize muscle engagement.
results.description: Barbell Bench Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Barbell Close Grip Bench Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor. Grip the barbell with your hands placed closer than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the barbell by extending your arms fully. Lower the barbell slowly and with control to your lower chest, keeping your elbows facing away from your body.
Press the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your arms fully, focusing on using your triceps and chest muscles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then carefully rack the barbell back onto the bench press rack.
tips: Maintain a controlled pace to ensure that you're using muscle strength rather than momentum.
Keep your feet flat on the floor to maintain stability and support your lower back.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you press the barbell up and inhaling as you lower it back down.
results.description: Barbell Close Grip Bench Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Barbell Floor Chest Press
instructions: Lie on your back on the floor with your feet flat on the floor. Grip a barbell with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, and hold the barbell directly above your chest with your arms bent, elbows on the floor.
Engage your core and slowly press the barbell up until your arms are straight over your chest.
Lower the barbell back to the starting position by bending your arms fully, focusing on using your chest muscles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Lower the barbell slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Ensure your elbows are at a 45-degree angle to your body to reduce shoulder strain.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you press the barbell up and inhaling as you lower it down.
results.description: Barbell Floor Chest Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Barbell Hooklying Bench Press Close Elbows
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your knees bent, feet resting on the bench, and grasp the barbell with a grip slightly narrower than shoulder width. Position the bar above your chest with your elbows tucked close to your sides.
Lower the barbell slowly toward the lower chest while keeping your elbows close to your torso.
Press the barbell upward by extending your elbows until your arms are fully straight above your chest.
Pause briefly at the top, slowly return to the starting position. Repeat while maintaining control throughout the movement.
tips: Keep your core engaged to stabilize your body on the bench.
Keep your elbows tucked in and maintain a neutral wrist position throughout the lift.
Press the bar vertically while keeping it balanced over your chest, while squeezing your triceps, and lower the bar under control, avoiding bouncing the weight off your chest.
Exhale as you press the bar upward and inhale as you lower it.
results.description: Barbell Hooklying Bench Press Close Elbows is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Serratus Anterior, Forearms.

results.name: Barbell Incline Bench Press

anatomical: Clavicular Head of the Pectoralis Major

instructions: Lie on an incline bench set at a 45 degree angle. Grip the barbell with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, and hold the barbell directly above your chest with your arms fully extended.
Slowly lower the barbell to your upper chest, keeping your elbows at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Press the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your arms fully, focusing on using your chest.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then carefully rack the barbell back onto the bench press rack.
tips: Breathe steadily, exhaling as you press the barbell up and inhaling as you lower it down.
Maintain a firm grip on the barbell to ensure control and proper alignment.
Use a spotter if lifting heavy weights to ensure safety.
results.description: Barbell Incline Bench Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Barbell JM Bench Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a barbell with your hands shoulder-width apart. Your arms should be fully extended above your chest.
Lower the barbell by bending your elbows and bringing it down towards your chest.
When the barbell is just above your chest, move it toward your head and stop when the barbell is just overhead and move it back to above the chest.

Push it back up to the starting position by extending your elbows, focusing on using your triceps. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then carefully rack the barbell back onto the bench press rack.
tips: Focus on the triceps by keeping your elbows slightly tucked in and not flaring out too much.
Lower the barbell slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Maintain a strong grip on the barbell to ensure control and proper alignment.
results.description: Barbell JM Bench Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Shoulders.

results.name: Barbell Landmine Chest Press
instructions: Stand facing the free end of the landmine barbell with your feet shoulder width apart and hold the end of the bar at chest height using both hands. Keep your elbows slightly in front of your body and brace your core.
Press the bar upward until your arms are fully extended while maintaining a stable, upright posture.
Pause briefly at the top while keeping your shoulders down and your chest engaged.
Slowly lower the bar back to chest level under control and repeat.
tips: Press the bar in its natural arc rather than trying to move it straight overhead.
Keep your elbows slightly tucked instead of flaring them outward.
Keep your core engaged and chest up, avoid leaning backward.
Exhale as you press the bar upward and inhale as you return.
results.description: Barbell Landmine Chest Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Serratus Anterior, Core.
